title: The Standoff Line — wildfire defence 30–100 m before the house
description: An automated wildfire defence line installed 30–100 metres ahead of homes. Engineered, costed and ready to build — we are looking for the partner who builds the first one.
hero_eyebrow: Wildfire defence engineering · Europe · USA · South-East Asia
hero_h1: Everyone protects the house. We stop the fire before it gets there.
hero_lead1: An automated defence line, 30 to 100 metres out: a continuous wet band that forms itself the moment a fire front approaches — on its own water, its own solar power, with a fluorine-free agent, and with nobody present.
hero_lead2: The engineering is done. The costs are modelled. What we are looking for is the partner who builds the first one.
hero_btn1: What we bring, what we need
gap_h2: Two questions decide everything: how far, and when.
gap_big: Every wildfire protection product on the market answers those two questions — and almost all of them answer both the same way: at the house, and once the fire is already there. Plot the field on those two axes and an empty square appears.

gap_figcaption: Where each approach acts. The treated strip is applied months ahead and degrades; the structure systems coat the house once the fire is already on the plot; mobile units have to arrive. The band at 30–100 m forms itself at the moment the front reaches it — and that square is empty today.

gap_note1_lead: We did not invent this idea, and we say so first.
gap_note1: In Spain, Medi XXI has built cannon-based perimeter defences around developments since 2006 and holds a granted patent. In France, STME FIRE runs a research programme on exactly this. In Portugal, university researchers ringed a village with twelve sprinkler columns in 2020. In the USA, two funded companies build barriers at industrial scale.
gap_note2: What is not being done is the part we built: a standoff line small enough, cheap enough and automatic enough to be bought by one house or one street — a continuous band from small heads instead of a few big cannons, dual-triggered, energy-independent, and with an agent that already meets the 2030 European ban on fluorinated foams.
sys_h2: A line that stands dry all year and wets itself in ninety seconds.
sys_c1_p: A brass impact head with a 15 m radius every 20 m, so the circles overlap into a 22 m unbroken wet band. At 10 m radius the band would have holes — and a fire goes through the holes.
sys_c2_p: A satellite fire alert arms the line at roughly 10 km. A local UV/IR flame detector fires it at roughly 300 m. Fast and precise, without choosing between them.
sys_c3_p: Own tank, own pump, solar with battery and an auto-start generator. At least four hours of operation. Mains water pressure and grid power are the first things a wildfire takes away.
sys_c4_p: A Class A foam measured below 1 mg/kg fluorine, GreenScreen Silver, and already on the US Forest Service qualified products list. It meets the 2030 EU PFAS ban today.
sys_c5_p: The flame detectors say which arc the front is coming from, so only that sector runs, plus two poles of margin. The water lasts two to three times longer.
sys_c6_p: Start time, pressure, water used, temperature, wind, runtime. Insurers price what they can model — so the line produces the evidence from its first day.
sys_p1_p: The line stands dry. A weekly self-test cycles the valves, the solar array keeps the battery full, the tank stays full. Nothing runs, nothing is wasted, and the same pipework can irrigate.
sys_p2_p: A satellite fire alert wakes the system. The pump pressurises, the sectors report ready, and the owner gets a notification — wherever they are.
sys_p3_p: Solar-powered UV/IR flame detector nodes along the line identify not only that a front is coming, but from which arc.
sys_p4_p: Only the threatened sector starts, plus two poles of margin. The overlapping heads build a continuous 22 m band; foam is dosed at 0.1–1%. In strong wind the controller switches to a coarser droplet so less of it drifts away.
sys_p5_p: At least four hours from its own tank. The active sector follows the front as it passes, and the band keeps cooling the ground after the flame has gone — which is what stops a re-ignition.
sys_p6_p: An event report: start time, runtime, pressures, water and agent used, temperature and wind. This is the file an insurer can model — and the reason the evidence exists from the first fire onwards.

Solar array, LiFePO4 battery in a fire-rated cabinet
Foam proportioner 0.1–1% and concentrate tank

num_note: Figures from our own hydraulic, energy and cost model, at European price levels. Distances: 30 m for grassland, 50 m for brush, a double row at 50 + 70 m for forest; roughly double on a slope the fire climbs.
sys_note: Up to 90% of homes lost in a wildfire are ignited by wind-driven embers, not by the flame front — and embers fly over any band. The line stops the front and takes away the radiant heat; ember-resistant vents, screens and a wetted roof stop the rest. We supply both, and we will never claim that one replaces the other.
dia_h2: Poles, not people. This is what stands there when nobody does.
dia_intro: There is no photograph of this system anywhere, because nobody is selling it yet — which is the whole reason this page exists. So here it is drawn: what one pole is made of, and what the ring does when a front arrives from one side.
d1_cap: One pole. A galvanised steel mast on a concrete footing, a brass impact head at the top with a 15 m throw, a solar UV/IR flame detector on the mast, and the HDPE main buried below the frost and plough line. Nothing here needs a person on the day.
d2_cap: The ring seen from above. Heads every 20 m, each throwing 15 m, so the circles overlap into one unbroken 22 m band. The detectors say which arc the front is coming from, and only that sector runs — plus two poles of margin on each side. That is what makes four hours of water last.
d2_margin: plus two poles of margin on each side
dia_note_lead: No installed reference exists — ours or anyone's.
dia_note: We have not built one yet, and we say so throughout this page. But the reason there is no photograph to show is not that the idea failed: it is that this square of the field is still empty. That is what we are asking a partner to help us change.
band_cap: A brass impact head, 15 m radius. One every 20 metres is what turns a row of sprinklers into an unbroken wet band.
off_h2: We are not asking for a job. We are bringing a project.
off_big: We can design it, size it, write its control software and manage its construction. What we cannot do is finance the first installation. That is the whole proposition, stated plainly.
off_bring1: A fully worked concept design — geometry, hydraulics, energy budget, tank sizing — ready for a licensed engineer to review and stamp
off_bring2: Control and sensing: dual trigger, sector logic, wind compensation, failsafes
off_bring3: The software — app, telemetry, event logging, the data package an insurer can model
off_bring4: The permitting dossier: visual impact, water discharge, environmental notes
off_bring5: Project direction by someone who has taken an industrial plant from the first meeting to handover
off_bring6: A competitor and patent analysis of the whole field, in writing
off_h3_need: What we need from a partner
off_need1: A site — a plot, a street, an estate, a utility corridor or a plant perimeter
off_need2: The capital for the first line. At demonstration length this is a small number
off_need3: The hydraulic and fire design has to be reviewed and stamped by a locally qualified engineer — we do not have that person, and we would rather say so than imply otherwise
off_need4: A locally licensed contractor, because the licence is always local: C-16 in California, Contractor II in Florida, RIPCI registration in Spain
off_need5: Permission to measure and publish what happens
off_who: Fire-protection and irrigation contractors · manufacturers looking for an application · utilities and railways · municipalities and fire districts · insurers and MGAs who already pay for mitigation · resorts, estates and industrial sites in fire-prone regions.
off_h3_first: The first step is small on purpose
off_first: A 100–200 metre demonstration line, instrumented, filmed, measured. We already have a candidate site: the perimeter of a six-hectare industrial plant in Vietnam — our own ground, our own crew, our own procurement. That is the cheapest credible proof in existence, and it is what turns a drawing into evidence.
off_note_lead: And the honest list of what we do not have.
off_note: No installed reference. No stamped fire-engineering design. No licence in any jurisdiction. What we do have is a concept worked through to cost level, the competitor and regulatory picture in writing, the software that makes it a defence line rather than a sprinkler, and a project director who has delivered before. We would rather open with that list than be found out holding it back.
team_h2: A project director, a systems engineer — and an honest list of what we are still missing.
p1_bio1: An economist by training who has taken projects from the first meeting to handover. General director (Tổng giám đốc) of an export poultry plant in Thanh Hóa province, Vietnam — built with Hungarian technology and Hungarian capital on a six-hectare site, and inaugurated on 24 October 2019 in the presence of the Hungarian and Vietnamese agriculture ministers and the Hungarian ambassador. Decades of international project management across two countries and two languages, and for many years a regular interpreter for high-level delegations of both governments, including the Vietnamese National Assembly delegation to Hungary in 2022.
p1_bio2_lead: He is not an engineer and does not present himself as one.
p1_bio2: What he brings is the thing most often missing on a build: that the project actually starts, that the parties pull in one direction, that the money and the schedule hold, and that somebody answers for the handover.
p2_bio1: Software and systems engineer: the sensing, the trigger logic, the sector control, the telemetry and the event log — and the application that lets an evacuating owner see that the line is alive. A former flight instructor, which is where the habit comes from of designing for the moment when something fails rather than the moment when everything works.
p2_bio2: In this system the software is not an accessory. The difference between a sprinkler and a defence line is what decides when it runs, how much water it spends, and what it can prove afterwards.
con_h2: Send us a site and a question. We will send back a design.
con_big: If you build fire protection, irrigation or infrastructure, and you have a perimeter that needs defending — that is the conversation we want. We answer in every language this page is written in.
con_note: The full concept study, the cost model and the competitor analysis are available on request, in Hungarian or English.
